tutorial.title: Gameplay Tutorial
tutorial.welcome: Welcome to KlassX Online! Let's walk through the basics to get you ready for action.
tutorial.movement: Use the joystick on the left side of your screen. Simply drag your thumb in any direction to move your character around the map.
tutorial.skill-buttons: These are your active Skill Buttons. Tap them during combat to unleash your abilities and combo attacks.
tutorial.skill-tab-switch: Need more abilities? Tap this button to instantly swap your active skill wheel between your first tab (slots 1-5) and your second tab (slots 6-10).
tutorial.skill-set-switch: Quickly adapt to any fight! Tap here to cycle through your 3 custom Skill Sets, allowing you to swap your entire build on the fly.
tutorial.stance: Control your pacing and readiness. Use these buttons to toggle your movement between Walk and Run, or switch your character's stance between Attack and Idle.
tutorial.main-menu-hold: Press and hold the Main Menu button to open the quick-access wheel. Just slide your finger to the bubble you want—like Character, Skills, or Inventory—and release to open it.
tutorial.upgrade-stats: Welcome to your Character Panel. As you level up, you'll earn stat points. Tap the plus (+) buttons next to your attributes to upgrade your stats and grow stronger.
tutorial.inventory-canvas: This is your Inventory. On the left, you can see your currently equipped gear. On the right is your bag space, your total Gold, and your 6 quick slots.
tutorial.skills-canvas: Here in the Skills Panel, you can view, manage, and arrange all the abilities you have unlocked so far.
tutorial.skill-details: Want to learn more about a specific ability? Tap any skill image to view its damage stats, cooldown times, and effects.
tutorial.skill-drag: To equip a skill, press and hold an icon from the Skill List on the left, then drag it directly into one of your active slots on the right. You have 10 slots arranged in 2 rows to customize your layout!
tutorial.skill-tab-difference: Use the Tab Switch within this panel to organize your layout. You can assign different abilities to your first page (1-5) and your second page (6-10).
tutorial.pots-slots: Notice the empty quick slots on your main screen? Before you can use HP or MP recovery items like Bread in combat, you need to open your Inventory to assign them.
tutorial.drag-pots: Inside your Inventory, just drag your recovery items onto any free quick slot. Potions share these six slots with your other items, so choose how many to spend on healing—and tapping a potion slot drinks it right away, with no confirmation to slow you down in a fight.

tutorial.pet-1: Welcome to the Pet System! Let's get your new companion ready. Tap on the highlighted Pet Icon in your inventory to view its details.
tutorial.pet-2: This is the Item Information panel. To summon your companion, simply click the Use button to equip them!
tutorial.pet-3: Look who's here! Your pet will now follow you on your adventures. To manage your new friend, click the Pet Button highlighted on your screen.
tutorial.pet-4: Welcome to the Pet Panel! This is where you can check on your companion's status, including their Name, Kind, and Food level. You start with one active Skill Slot—but don't worry, you can unlock the second one later by finding and using a Pet dual skill card.
tutorial.pet-5: Let's get your pet ready for action. Open the Skill Dropdown to view all currently learned skills, and select the one you want to equip.
tutorial.pet-6: Pets need constant care and training to grow stronger! To get items like Pet Food and Pet Skills, you'll need to head out into the world and grind for them. Check your inventory to see what you've collected so far.
tutorial.pet-7: To teach your companion a new trick, select a Pet Skill item and click Use. Note: Your pet must be currently equipped to learn a new skill!
tutorial.pet-8: Adventures make pets hungry! Select the Pet Food item and click Use to feed your currently equipped companion.
tutorial.pet-9: Great job! As you can see back in the Pet Panel, your pet's HP bar is full. A well-fed pet is a happy pet!
tutorial.pet-10: Need to travel solo or switch companions? Simply click your pet's icon in the inventory and press the Unuse button to unequip them safely.
tutorial.item-upgrades-1: Ready to forge stronger gear? To get started, tap the highlighted Inventory button on your screen to open your inventory.
tutorial.item-upgrades-2: Here in your inventory, you can see all the items we'll be working with. You have a Fine Burr for upgrading weapons, a Wood Sword, a Luxury Protection Potion for armor, a piece of Armor, and a Costume.
tutorial.item-upgrades-3: Let's upgrade your weapon first! Select the Fine Burr to open its Item Information panel, then click the Use button. This will bring up the Upgrade Panel.
tutorial.item-upgrades-4: Welcome to the Upgrade Panel! Notice that the Fine Burr has automatically been placed into its slot. Below, you will see the Close and Upgrade buttons.
tutorial.item-upgrades-5: Take a look at the highlighted areas. These are your two main slots: on the left side is for the gear you want to upgrade, and the right side holds your upgrade material.
tutorial.item-upgrades-6: Now, let's prepare your weapon. Hold and drag the Wood Sword from your inventory and drop it directly into the weapon slot in the Upgrade Panel.
tutorial.item-upgrades-7: Time to forge! Click the Upgrade button. If the process is successful, your item's power will increase, indicated by a plus sign and a number on the item icon—just like this +3!
tutorial.item-upgrades-8: Let's move on to your defense. Back in your inventory, select the Luxury Protection Potion and click the Use button to open the Upgrade Panel for your armor.
tutorial.item-upgrades-9: Just like you did with the weapon, drag your Armor from the inventory straight into the empty slot in the Upgrade Panel to prepare it for enhancement.
tutorial.merge-1: Want to upgrade your look while keeping your heavy stats? You can combine armor and costumes! Simply drag your Costume and drop it directly on top of your Armor in the inventory. A Merge Panel will pop up asking, 'Do you want to combine costume?' Click Yes to fuse them.
tutorial.merge-2: Success! Your newly merged armor is now equipped. You keep all the defensive stats of your upgraded armor, but your character now shows off the stylish costume. You are ready for battle!
tutorial.interaction-1: To interact with others in the world, first select a player. Once selected, tap and hold the highlighted Player Interaction button to reveal your options.
tutorial.interaction-2: Here are your Player Interaction options! From this menu, you can choose various ways to interact with your selected target.
tutorial.interaction-3: Let's start with private messaging. Tap the highlighted Whisper button to open your main chat window, which will automatically switch to the Whisper category.
tutorial.interaction-4: Notice that the chat input field has automatically added the '@' symbol followed by the player's name. Just type your message and hit enter to talk privately!
tutorial.interaction-5: Want to exchange items? Tap the Trade button. This sends a request to the other player. If they accept, the Trade Panel will open for both of you.
tutorial.interaction-6: Welcome to the Trade Panel! The top slots belong to the other player, and the bottom slots are yours. To offer an item—like this Bread—simply drag it from your inventory into your bottom slots. Once you are happy with your offer, click the Lock button.
tutorial.interaction-7: After locking your items, the Accept button will be enabled. Both players must click Accept for the trade to succeed. If you change your mind, just hit Refuse to cancel the transaction.
tutorial.interaction-8: Looking to recruit? The Club Invite button sends a club invitation to the selected player. Note: You must be the Guild Master or have an Inviter role to use this feature!
tutorial.interaction-9: To manage your club, open your main Menu and tap the highlighted Club button.
tutorial.interaction-10: This is the Main Club Panel. By tapping the Notice button, you can view the club's announcements below. If you are the Guild Master, you can edit this text to keep your members updated.
tutorial.interaction-11: Switching to the Member tab shows everyone in your Club. Next to their names, you'll find management buttons allowing you to pass Guild Master leadership, assign roles, invite them to a party, or kick/leave the club.
tutorial.interaction-12: Make new friends by tapping the Add Friend button in the interaction menu. This will instantly send a friend request to the selected player.
tutorial.interaction-13: To view your friends, open the main Menu again and tap the Friends button.
tutorial.interaction-14: Here in the Main Friends Panel, you can keep track of your friends. Use the buttons next to their names to Whisper, Teleport directly to them (requires a Teleport Card), Remove them as a friend, or Block them.
tutorial.interaction-15: Ready for a challenge? Tap the Duel button to open the customization panel.
tutorial.interaction-16: Here you can set the rules for your fight: toggle Recovery Dose usage, adjust HP boosts, and restrict the combat range. Click OK to send the challenge and wait for them to accept!
tutorial.interaction-17: Team up by tapping the Party button.
tutorial.interaction-18: A customization panel will appear where you can set rules, like how dropped items and coins are allocated among members. Set your preferences and click OK to send the party invite.
tutorial.interaction-19: Once they accept, a Mini Party panel will appear on the left side of your screen showing active members. You can quickly target an ally by tapping their HP bar—perfect for classes like the Shaman who need to cast buffs quickly! To hide this panel, simply swipe it to the left.
tutorial.interaction-20: When the panel is hidden, a Show Party button will appear on the edge of the screen. Just tap it whenever you want to bring the Mini Party panel back.
tutorial.interaction-21: For more advanced party options, open your Menu and select the Party button.
tutorial.interaction-22: Welcome to the Main Party Panel. If you are the Party Leader, you'll see options to Disb (disband the entire party), Assist (transfer leadership to another player), or Leave (kick a selected member). If you are a regular member, you will only see the Leave button to exit the party yourself.
tutorial.macro-1: Welcome to the Macro System! To quickly send pre-set messages, locate the encircled Macro button on your main screen. Tap and hold this button to reveal your available macros—they will pop up just like your menu and player interaction options!
tutorial.macro-2: Once the menu expands, you will see all of your available macro buttons displayed. Simply tap the specific macro you want to trigger to instantly send the message.
tutorial.macro-3: Want to customize your quick messages? Open your Menu, go to Options, select the Game tab, and tap the Edit Macro button to get started.
tutorial.macro-4: This is the Macro Edit screen, where all your custom messages are stored. Tap on the highlighted first macro slot to begin modifying its contents.
tutorial.macro-5: Now you can type out your custom shout-out or command! Please note that your custom macro message has a maximum limit of 75 characters, and emojis are not allowed.
tutorial.macro-6: Need your Macro button in a more comfortable spot? Head back to the Game Options menu and select the highlighted Custom UI Layout button to adjust your on-screen controls.
tutorial.macro-7: In the layout editor, tap the Macro button to adjust its scale and opacity.
tutorial.macro-8: To change its position, simply drag the icon across the screen. Note: The macro button remains fully active during editing, so its sub-menu might pop up while you are dragging it around!
tutorial.quest-1: Welcome to the Quest System! Outside of grinding, quests are your most reliable source of EXP and rewards. This guide walks you through finding the quest NPC, accepting a quest, keeping track of your progress, and turning the quest in to claim your reward.
tutorial.quest-2: This is the New Quest Helper, the NPC who hands out the quest line. Take note of the level requirement: quests are level-gated, and this chain only begins at level 39. Talk to the NPC before that and no quest option will appear at all, because an NPC only offers what you already qualify for. Each following quest in the line unlocks roughly every 10 levels, so come back as you grow stronger.
tutorial.quest-3: Talking to the NPC opens the dialogue panel, which lists every option you currently qualify for. Here the Rank 5 Spiritual Sphere quest is on offer, the first quest of the chain and the one unlocked at level 39. Tap it to accept. Once accepted the option disappears from the list, and quests you are already on or have already finished are hidden here too.
tutorial.quest-4: You do not have to run back to the NPC just to check what you are working on. Open your Menu and tap the Quest button to bring up your Quest Log at any time.
tutorial.quest-5: The Quest Log has two tabs. Ongoing lists every quest you are currently on, such as the Rank 5 Spiritual Sphere you just accepted. A quest only moves to the Completed tab after you hand it in to the NPC, not the moment you finish its objectives.
tutorial.quest-6: Tap a quest to open its full details: the description, the objectives you need to clear, and the rewards waiting for you. Objectives that ask you to defeat enemies show a live count such as (3/10) and are ticked off once the count is full. Reaching the full count does not end the quest. Return to the NPC and choose the Complete option to hand it in and receive your rewards. Give Up removes the quest for good, and most quests cannot be taken a second time.

help.consumable.title: Quick Slots
help.consumable.s1.heading: What goes here
help.consumable.s1.body: Six slots for the items you reach for most — potions, pet cards, Back Point and Start Point passes, teleport and entry cards, locker cards, store permits and Fate Boxes. Everything shares these six slots.
help.consumable.s2.heading: Assigning an item
help.consumable.s2.body: Open your bag and drag an item onto an empty slot. If a slot refuses the item, that type is not supported here — use it from your bag instead.
help.consumable.s3.heading: Using an item
help.consumable.s3.body: Tap a filled slot to use it. Potions are drunk immediately with no confirmation so they work in a fight. Everything else asks to confirm first, and the usual rules still apply: a pet cannot be summoned on a map that disallows pets, and a Back Point pass needs a back point on record.
help.consumable.s4.heading: Clearing a slot
help.consumable.s4.body: Tap the item icon inside a slot to unbind it — the item stays in your bag. A slot also clears itself once you run out of that item.
help.consumable.s5.heading: Cooldowns
help.consumable.s5.body: The dark sweep across a slot is that item's cooldown. Cooldowns follow the item, not the slot, so the same sweep appears in your bag at the same time.
help.consumable.s6.heading: Saving
help.consumable.s6.body: Your slot setup is saved per character on this device, so it is still here the next time you log in.
help.potion.title: Potions and Auto Potion
help.potion.s1.heading: Where potions go
help.potion.s1.body: There is no separate potion bar any more. Potions share the same six quick slots as everything else — drag a potion from your bag onto any free slot, and you decide how many of the six to give up to healing.
help.potion.s2.heading: Using a potion
help.potion.s2.body: Tap the slot to drink at once — potions never ask for confirmation. The number on the slot is your total of that potion across the whole bag, not just one stack, so the slot keeps working as stacks run down.
help.potion.s3.heading: Clearing a slot
help.potion.s3.body: Tap the potion icon inside a slot to unbind it and free the slot for something else. A slot also clears itself once the last potion is gone.
help.potion.s4.heading: Auto Potion
help.potion.s4.body: Switch on Auto Potion to drink from your quick slots automatically whenever your HP, MP or SP drops below the thresholds you set. It only ever uses slots holding a potion and ignores the rest. Auto Potion stays off during duels, and potions that restore HP cannot be used on the Tyranny map.
help.inventory.title: Using Your Inventory
help.inventory.s1.heading: Tap an item
help.inventory.s1.body: Opens its details with an action button that matches the item — Equip, Use, Preview, or Unequip when tapped from your equipment. With a shop open the button becomes Sell.
help.inventory.s2.heading: Hold an item
help.inventory.s2.body: Hold a stacked item to split it, then enter how many to move into a new stack.
help.inventory.s3.heading: Move and stack
help.inventory.s3.body: Drag an item onto another slot to swap the two, or onto a matching stack to combine them.
help.inventory.s4.heading: Drop an item
help.inventory.s4.body: Drag an item outside the bag to drop it on the ground.
help.inventory.s5.heading: Drag onto an open window
help.inventory.s5.body: Drag into a shop to sell, into a trade window to offer, into the upgrade window to refine, or into your locker to store it.
help.inventory.s6.heading: Cards used on other items
help.inventory.s6.body: Some items work by dragging them onto a target in your bag: Pet Food onto a Pet Card to feed it, a Garbage Card onto an item to destroy it, a Non-Drop Card onto equipment to protect it, a Wrapper onto bound equipment to make it tradeable again, and a costume onto matching equipment to change its look. A Detergent removes a costume that has already been applied.
help.inventory.s7.heading: Quick slots
help.inventory.s7.body: Drag potions and utility items onto your six quick slots for one-tap access without opening your bag.
help.all.title: Inventory Guide
help.quests.title: Quests
help.quests.s1.heading: Ongoing and Completed
help.quests.s1.body: The Ongoing tab lists the quests you are currently on. A quest only moves to the Completed tab after you hand it in.
help.quests.s2.heading: Tap a quest
help.quests.s2.body: Opens its details: the steps you need to finish and the rewards waiting for you.
help.quests.s3.heading: Tracking your progress
help.quests.s3.body: Objectives that need you to defeat enemies show a live count such as (3/10). A step is ticked off once its count is full.
help.quests.s4.heading: Finishing a quest
help.quests.s4.body: Reaching the full count does not end the quest on its own. Return to the NPC who gave it to you and choose the Complete option to hand it in.
help.quests.s5.heading: Rewards
help.quests.s5.body: Rewards are handed over only when you turn the quest in, so nothing arrives in your bag before then. Tap any reward icon to see what the item is.
help.quests.s6.heading: Giving up
help.quests.s6.body: Giving up removes the quest for good. Most quests cannot be taken a second time, so only give up if you are sure.
help.quests.s7.heading: Finding new quests
help.quests.s7.body: Talk to NPCs to pick up quests. An NPC only offers what you qualify for, so a quest you cannot see yet may need a higher level, a different class, or another quest finished first.
help.quests.s8.heading: When quests open up
help.quests.s8.body: The quest line currently begins at level 39, so characters below that level won't find any quests to pick up yet — that's expected, not a bug. Once you reach 39, a new quest unlocks roughly every 10 levels after that as you keep progressing.
help.guild.title: Guilds
help.guild.s1.heading: What a guild is
help.guild.s1.body: A guild is a roster of players who share a name, a notice board, and a chat channel. Every guild starts at Level 1 with room for 16 members.
help.guild.s2.heading: Upgrading your guild
help.guild.s2.body: Only the guild master can upgrade the guild, and it's done by talking to the designated rank-up NPC — not from a menu. Each upgrade raises the guild's level, its member cap, and the requirements for the next one, so upgrades get more expensive as you go.
help.guild.s3.heading: What an upgrade costs
help.guild.s3.body: Every upgrade needs two things: the guild master's own character must be at or above the required level, and the guild must pay the gold cost in full. Both are checked before the upgrade goes through.
help.guild.s4.heading: Member cap by level
help.guild.s4.body:
Level 1: 16 members (starting size)
Level 2: 20 members - master level 45, 2,000,000 gold
Level 3: 30 members - master level 60, 3,500,000 gold
Level 4: 40 members - master level 80, 5,000,000 gold
Level 5: 60 members - master level 100, 7,000,000 gold
Level 6: 80 members - master level 120, 10,000,000 gold (max level)
help.guild.s5.heading: Alliances
help.guild.s5.body: A guild can also form an alliance with other guilds, which shares a separate roster from your guild's own member cap. Alliances are managed by the guild master from the guild panel.
help.report.title: Reporting a Bug
help.report.s1.heading: Where reports go
help.report.s1.body: Bugs and support requests are handled through our website, not inside the game. Reports raised there reach the team directly and can be followed up on.
help.report.s2.heading: Step 1 - Log in
help.report.s2.body: Open the website and log in with the same account you use to play.
help.report.s3.heading: Step 2 - Go to Tickets
help.report.s3.body: Open the Tickets section of your account.
help.report.s4.heading: Step 3 - Submit a ticket
help.report.s4.body: Choose Bug Report for something broken in the game, or General Support for account, payment and other questions.
help.report.s5.heading: What to include
help.report.s5.body: Tell us what you were doing, what you expected to happen, and what happened instead. Add your character name, the map you were on, and roughly when it happened.
help.report.s6.heading: Screenshots help
help.report.s6.body: Attach a screenshot or a short video if you can. Being able to see the problem is the fastest way for us to reproduce and fix it.
